## Font File Preview (FS)

The font family's renderer. **The browser is the decoder**: `applyFileFont` loads the linked face onto the specimen container and every sample below inherits it — so what you see is the real typeface, not a description of it.

### Each format gets a different amount of the specimen, on one load

| Format | What it shows |
|---|---|
| fitted | a single showcase glyph |
| embedded | compact name plus pangram |
| isolated | full waterfall + character map |

All three share **one FontFace load**. The specimen scales, the cost does not.

### Two deliberate typographic choices

**The pangram is a type designer's, not "quick brown fox".** It covers every letter *and* mixes shapes that expose a face's personality faster than the familiar sentence does.

**The waterfall is reading sizes, not display sizes.** Large enough at the top to read the letterforms, small enough at the bottom to prove the face still holds up as body text — which is the question someone evaluating a font actually has.


Projected into the four format shells by `FilePreviewStage`, which owns the loading, failure and staleness panes — this component draws content only.
